name: Gold
spiritual: Associated with the sun and illumination
Stimulates the solar plexus and crown
physical: Traditionally associated with vitality and warmth
Kept nearby for energy and radiance
Folk traditions link it to a feeling of wellbeing
summary: Native gold is the radiant, untarnishing metal found as nuggets and crystals, a symbol of the sun, abundance, confidence and incorruptible self-worth.
intro: Native gold is the real thing: soft, heavy, buttery-yellow metal found as nuggets, wire-like crystals, flakes in quartz and dust in river gravel. It is the only yellow metal that does not tarnish, and it can be hammered thin enough to see light through. Crystal gold, in tiny octahedra and branching forms, is rare and prized by collectors, while quartz with visible gold is a beloved specimen. Gold is 2.5 to 3 on the Mohs scale, extremely malleable and dense. It has been a symbol of wealth and divinity for as long as people have known it, and crystal healers treat it as the metal of the sun.
history: Gold has been used for ornament for at least 6,000 years, with some of the oldest gold treasures from Varna in Bulgaria. Egyptians associated gold with the flesh of the gods, and pharaohs were buried in gold masks. Gold standards underpinned currencies, and gold rushes in California, Australia, South Africa and Alaska reshaped history. Alchemists believed gold to be the perfect metal, the goal of transmutation. The symbol of gold is the sun in alchemical tradition. Today it is used in jewelry, electronics and investment, and as a crystal specimen it represents purity and abundance.
meaning: In crystal and alchemical tradition gold is the sun metal: radiance, confidence, generosity and incorruptible worth. It is linked to the solar plexus, heart and crown chakras. Practitioners say it helps people feel centered in their own value, shine without ego and attract abundance. Gold in quartz is a particularly treasured combination, joining clarity with prosperity. Emotionally it is said to lift a dim mood and bring warmth and self-respect. Traditionally it is associated with vitality and a bright sense of wellbeing, though only as lore. For many, a small piece of gold jewelry or specimen is a personal talisman of success.
howToUse: Wear gold jewelry or hold a small gold specimen during intention-setting about worth and abundance. Place a piece of gold-in-quartz on your desk or altar to emphasize clarity and prosperity. In a grid, set gold at the center with citrine and pyrite. A small nugget or ring can be held during moments of doubt, as a reminder of your radiance. Place a specimen in the southeast of the home for wealth energy.
care: Gold does not tarnish and is very easy to care for. A quick wash in mild soapy water and a soft cloth keeps it bright. It is soft, so avoid abrasive cleaners and store separately from harder stones. Cleanse with sound, smoke, moonlight or sunlight. Specimens with quartz or matrix should be dusted gently. Keep specimens in a small padded box to avoid scratching.
identify: Real gold is heavy, soft and bendable, with a buttery yellow color and a gold-colored streak. Pyrite and chalcopyrite look similar but are brittle, harder and leave dark streaks. Gold flakes sink in water, while mica flakes float. Brass and gold-plated metals can also mimic it. A simple test is to cut or scratch the surface: real gold shows the same color beneath.

faq.q: What does gold symbolize in crystal healing?
faq.a: Gold symbolizes the sun, radiance, confidence and abundance. In crystal tradition it is linked to the solar plexus and crown and used to support self-worth and success.

faq.q: How can I tell real gold from pyrite?
faq.a: Real gold is soft, malleable and heavy, with a gold-colored streak, while pyrite is brittle, harder and leaves a greenish-black streak. Pyrite also shows sharp cubic crystals and may strike sparks against steel.
Yes. Gold is inert and can be washed in mild soapy water. Dry it with a soft cloth, and be careful with specimens that include matrix or other minerals that may be fragile.
